claims.source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014.

claims.claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors.
claims.source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cai et al., 2011.

claims.claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of serotonin (5-HT) receptors.
claims.source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Joubert et al., 2004.

claims.claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3).
claims.source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lunn et al., 2007.

claims.claim: SNX27 is required to maintain AMPA-receptor-mediated postsynaptic currents during the process of synaptic plasticity.
claims.source: From studies in SNX27 knockout mice, it is clear that SNX27 is required to maintain AMPA-receptor-mediated postsynaptic currents during the process of synaptic plasticity (Wang et al., 2013; Loo et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2013; Loo et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2011.

claims.claim: De-regulation of SNX27 expression associated with Down's syndrome is considered to lead to synaptic dysfunction, in part, through reduced SNX27-mediated AMPA receptor trafficking.
claims.source: Indeed, the de-regulation of SNX27 expression associated with Down's syndrome (Wang et al., 2013), is considered to lead to synaptic dysfunction, in part, through reduced SNX27-mediated AMPA receptor trafficking.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013 and represents an interpretation of the data.

claims.claim: Clairfeuille and colleagues were unable to detect quantifiable binding of SNX27 to the AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2 using isothermal titration calorimetry.
claims.source: However, using isothermal titration calorimetry Clairfeuille and colleagues were unable to detect quantifiable binding of SNX27 to the AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2.
claims.evidence: This statement refers to experimental results from Clairfeuille and colleagues.

claims.claim: Clairfeuille and colleagues failed to observe binding between SNX27 and GluA1 upon GluA1 phosphorylation.
claims.source: Moreover, the authors failed to observe binding upon GluA1 phosphorylation, or upon association of SNX27 with the retromer component VPS26, which is known to enhance SNX27 binding to other PDZ binding motif-containing cargoes (Clairfeuille et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement refers to experimental results from Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Association of SNX27 with the retromer component VPS26 is known to enhance SNX27 binding to other PDZ binding motif-containing cargoes.
claims.source: Moreover, the authors failed to observe binding upon GluA1 phosphorylation, or upon association of SNX27 with the retromer component VPS26, which is known to enhance SNX27 binding to other PDZ binding motif-containing cargoes (Clairfeuille et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claims.claim: GFP-SNX27 retains the ability to localise to endosomes as defined by co-localisation with the early endosomal marker EEA1.
claims.source: Here, we transduced cortical neurons with sindbis virus expressing either GFP or GFP-SNX27 and verified that the GFP-SNX27 retained the ability to localise to endosomes as defined by co-localisation with the early endosomal marker EEA1 (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: 276 proteins were initially identified as SNX27-interacting proteins by excluding proteins not present in all three datasets.
claims.source: A single list of SNX27-interacting proteins (276 proteins) was initially resolved by excluding proteins not present in all three datasets (Figure 1B and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This statement describes the initial filtering of proteomic data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: 212 proteins comprise a high confidence cortical neuronal SNX27 interactome after further refinement.
claims.source: We further refined these data by excluding proteins that had an average log-fold change of GFP-SNX27:GFP of less than two and removed identified proteins if they did not meet statistical significance (p<0.05). The resulting 212 proteins were considered to comprise a high confidence cortical neuronal SNX27 interactome (Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This statement describes the refined proteomic data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Established SNX27 interactors including the retromer and WASH complexes were identified in the proteomic screen.
claims.source: Confirming the validity of our approach, many established SNX27 interactors were identified including the retromer and WASH complexes (Steinberg et al., 2013) and OTU deubiquitinase with linear linkage specificity (OTULIN) – a deubiquitinase with specificity for Met1-linked ubiquitin chains (Stangl et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Steinberg et al., 2013 and Stangl et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Many of the SNX27 interactors were classified as having a role in neuronal development and differentiation, as well as intracellular transport.
claims.source: We used gene ontology analysis (PANTHER Classification System; p < 0.05) to assess the neuronal SNX27 interactome and found that many of the SNX27 interactors were classified in having a role in neuronal development and differentiation, as well as intracellular transport (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Sixteen out of 212 identified proteins contained a Type I PDZ binding motif with the optimal acidic amino acid at the −3 position required for high-affinity binding to SNX27.
claims.source: Out of the 212 identified proteins sixteen contained a Type I PDZ binding motif with the optimal acidic amino acid at the −3 position required for high-affinity binding to SNX27 (Clairfeuille et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Seven proteins with Type I PDZ binding motifs were classified as integral proteins: SLC1A3, SLC4A7, SLC6A11, KCNT2, KIDINS220, ADAM22, and LRFN2.
claims.source: Within this cohort, seven proteins were classified as integral proteins (shown in orange in Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1): the high-affinity glutamate transporter, SLC1A3 (Storck et al., 1992) (PDZ binding motif – E−3-T-K-M−0) and the sodium bicarbonate co-transporter, SLC4A7 (Thornell and Bevensee, 2015) (E−3-T-S-L−0); a sodium-dependent transporter, SLC6A11 (Borden, 1996) (E−3-T-H-F−0); an outward rectifying potassium channel, KCNT2 (Bhattacharjee et al., 2003) (E−3-T-Q-L−0); a scaffold in neurotrophin signalling, KIDINS220 (Iglesias et al., 2000; Kong et al., 2001) (E−3-S-I-L−0); a receptor for the neuronal secreted protein LGI1 (Fukata, 2006), ADAM22 (E−3-T-S-I−0), and LRFN2 (E−3-S-T-V−0), a protein previously implicated in the synaptic clustering of glutamate receptors (Ko et al., 2006; Morimura et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006), and genetically associated with patients harbouring working memory deficits (Thevenon et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations and refers to Figure 1C.

claims.claim: AMPA receptor subunits were not classified as components of the neuronal SNX27 interactome.
claims.source: Interestingly, we failed to classify any AMPA receptor subunits as components of the neuronal SNX27 interactome.
claims.evidence: This is a direct statement about the proteomic results.

claims.claim: GluA2 was quantified in one data set but did not fulfil the stringent filtering criteria.
claims.source: That said, GluA2 was quantified in one data set but did not fulfil the stringent filtering criteria and hence was not annotated in the final interactome.
claims.evidence: This is a direct statement about the proteomic results.

claims.claim: GFP-SLC1A3 and GFP-SLC4A7 efficiently pulled down endogenous SNX27 in a manner dependent on their PDZ binding motifs.
claims.source: While both GFP-SLC1A3 and GFP-SLC4A7 efficiently pulled down endogenous SNX27, in a manner dependent on their PDZ binding motifs (Figure 1F), we failed to observe detectable association of endogenous SNX27 with any of the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor subunits (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: No detectable association of endogenous SNX27 with any of the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor subunits was observed in HEK293T cells.
claims.source: While both GFP-SLC1A3 and GFP-SLC4A7 efficiently pulled down endogenous SNX27, in a manner dependent on their PDZ binding motifs (Figure 1F), we failed to observe detectable association of endogenous SNX27 with any of the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor subunits (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: No association of AMPA receptor subunits with rat SNX27 was observed in HEK293T cells expressing Flag-tagged full-length rat SNX27.
claims.source: To ensure that the lack of detectable binding did not arise from species cross reactivity, an unlikely event given the high-sequence conservation between rat and human SNX27, we also performed a series of co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293T cells expressing the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor carboxy-terminal tails and Flag-tagged full-length rat SNX27. Again, we failed to observe a detectable association of AMPA receptor subunits with rat SNX27 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: No association of endogenous GluA1 or GluA2 with rat SNX27 was detected in primary rat cortical neuronal cultures.
claims.source: Finally, to examine whether SNX27 could potentially interact with AMPA receptors specifically in the context of neurons we transduced primary rat cortical neuronal cultures with sindbis virus expressing either GFP or GFP-SNX27. Twenty-four hr after transduction we carried out GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation and quantitative western blotting for the endogenous AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2. Again, under these conditions, we failed to detect any association of endogenous GluA1 or GluA2 with rat SNX27 (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: The data is consistent with the SNX27-dependent recycling of AMPA receptors being principally controlled by indirect binding.
claims.source: Together these data are consistent with the AMPA receptor PDZ binding motifs lacking the optimal sequence for high-affinity SNX27 binding (Clairfeuille et al., 2016) and corroborate our proteomic data. Whilst our data do not exclude that SNX27 may directly bind to AMPA receptors under specific circumstances, our data is more consistent with the SNX27-dependent recycling of AMPA receptors being principally controlled by indirect binding.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data and is supported by a citation to Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claims.claim: LRFN2 is a protein known to be involved in synaptic clustering.
claims.source: Of particular interest in this regard was LRFN2, a protein known to be involved in synaptic clustering (Ko et al., 2006; Morimura et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Ko et al., 2006; Morimura et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006.

claims.claim: The LRFN family comprises five single transmembrane spanning proteins, LRFN1 through to LRFN5.
claims.source: The LRFN family (also known as synaptic adhesion-like molecules [SALMs]) comprises five single transmembrane spanning proteins, LRFN1 through to LRFN5, that each contain an extracellular region of six leucine-rich repeats (LRR), an immunoglobulin (Ig) domain and a fibronectin type III domain, but differ in their cytosolic facing carboxy-terminal tails with LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 containing a Type I PDZ binding motif (Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008.

claims.claim: LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 contain a Type I PDZ binding motif.
claims.source: The LRFN family (also known as synaptic adhesion-like molecules [SALMs]) comprises five single transmembrane spanning proteins, LRFN1 through to LRFN5, that each contain an extracellular region of six leucine-rich repeats (LRR), an immunoglobulin (Ig) domain and a fibronectin type III domain, but differ in their cytosolic facing carboxy-terminal tails with LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 containing a Type I PDZ binding motif (Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008.

claims.claim: LRFN1 and LRFN4 were identified in the raw SNX27 proteomic data sets but were filtered out from the final high confidence interactome because they were not quantified across all three biological repeats.
claims.source: Both LRFN1 and LRFN4 were identified in the raw SNX27 proteomic data sets but were each filtered out from the final high confidence interactome because they were not quantified across all three biological repeats (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is a direct statement about the proteomic results.

claims.claim: Only those LRFNs containing a PDZ binding motif, LRFN1, LRFN2 and LRFN4, associated with endogenous SNX27.
claims.source: Transient transfection into HEK293T cells followed by GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation of the GFP-LRFN fusion proteins and quantitative western blotting revealed that only those LRFNs containing a PDZ binding motif, LRFN1, LRFN2 and LRFN4, associated with endogenous SNX27 (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Each association between LRFNs and SNX27 was dependent on the presence of the corresponding PDZ binding motif.
claims.source: Moreover, each association was dependent on the presence of the corresponding PDZ binding motif as deletion of the last three amino acids resulted in mutant LRFNs that failed to associate with SNX27 (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Mutation of the glutamic acid residue at the −3 position (LRFN2 (p.E786A)) or the carboxy-terminal valine (LRFN2 (p.V789A)) lead to the formation of mutant proteins that each lost the ability to associate with SNX27.
claims.source: The LRFN2 PDZ binding motif is defined by the sequence E−3-S−2-T−1-V0, where the valine residue constitutes the carboxy-terminal amino acid. Mutation of the glutamic acid residue at the −3 position (LRFN2 (p.E786A)) or the carboxy-terminal valine (LRFN2 (p.V789A)) lead to the formation of mutant proteins that each lost the ability to associate with SNX27 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: The isolated recombinant PDZ domain of SNX27 directly bound to a synthetic peptide corresponding to the LRFN2 PDZ binding motif with a high micromolar affinity (Kd = 1.6 µM).
claims.source: This established that the isolated recombinant PDZ domain of SNX27 directly bound to a synthetic peptide corresponding to the LRFN2 PDZ binding motif, S-S-E-W-V-M-E−3-S-T-V−0 with a high micromolar affinity (Kd = 1.6 µM) (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The affinity of the interaction between SNX27 PDZ domain and LRFN2 PDZ binding motif was enhanced upon inclusion of recombinant VPS26 (Kd < 1.0 µM).
claims.source: Moreover, the affinity of this interaction was enhanced upon inclusion of recombinant VPS26 (Kd < 1.0 µM), a retromer component that directly associates with the PDZ domain of SNX27 and has been previously shown to enhance the binding affinity between the SNX27 PDZ domain and PDZ binding motif-containing peptides (Gallon et al., 2014; Chan et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2D and citations to Gallon et al., 2014; Chan et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Endogenous LRFN2 associated with SNX27 in primary rat cortical neuronal cultures.
claims.source: Finally, to confirm that endogenous LRFN2 also associated with SNX27, we transduced primary rat cortical neuronal cultures with sindbis virus expressing either GFP or GFP-SNX27. GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation and quantitative western blotting confirmed the association between SNX27 and full-length endogenous LRFN2 (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: By means of its carboxy-terminal PDZ binding motif LRFN2 directly associates with the PDZ domain of SNX27.
claims.source: Together these data establish that by means of its carboxy-terminal PDZ binding motif LRFN2 directly associates with the PDZ domain of SNX27.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: The endosome associated SNX27 co-localised with LRFN2 punctae throughout the neuron including in the dendrites and the cell body.
claims.source: Confocal microscopy revealed that the endosome associated SNX27 (see Figure 1A) co-localised with LRFN2 punctae throughout the neuron including in the dendrites and the cell body (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The suppression of SNX27 expression led to a robust reduction in the total cellular level of LRFN2 (an approximate 50% reduction).
claims.source: Similar to a wide array of other integral proteins that require endosomal SNX27 for their retrieval away from the lysosomal degradative fate (Steinberg et al., 2013), the suppression of SNX27 expression led to a robust reduction in the total cellular level of LRFN2 (an approximate 50% reduction, n = 5, unpaired t-test, t (8) = 4.6, p = 0.0017) (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and a citation to Steinberg et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA1 (an approximate 37% reduction).
claims.source: Consistent with published studies (Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013), the suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA1 and GluA2 (an approximate 37% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.9, p = 0.0078; and an approximate 64% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 4.0, p = 0.0074) (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and citations to Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA2 (an approximate 64% reduction).
claims.source: Consistent with published studies (Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013), the suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA1 and GluA2 (an approximate 37% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.9, p = 0.0078; and an approximate 64% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 4.0, p = 0.0074) (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and citations to Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Transferrin receptor levels were unchanged after SNX27 suppression.
claims.source: Transferrin receptor levels were also measured as a control and were found to be unchanged (n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 0.6, p = 0.5774) (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: SNX27 suppression induced a robust reduction in the cell surface level of LRFN2 (an approximate 52% reduction).
claims.source: Importantly, under these conditions, SNX27 suppression also induced a robust reduction in the cell surface level of LRFN2 (an approximate 52% reduction, n = 6, unpaired t-test, t (10) = 5.0, p = 0.0006) (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: The colocalisation between LRFN2 and LAMP2 significantly increased after SNX27 suppression (an approximate 27% increase).
claims.source: The colocalisation between LRFN2 and LAMP2 significantly increased after SNX27 suppression (an approximate 27% increase, n = 30, unpaired t-test, t (58) = 2.4, p = 0.0200) (Figure 3G).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: LRFN2 is an integral protein that requires SNX27 for its retrieval from lysosomal degradation, a pre-requisite for recycling back to the cell surface.
claims.source: Together these data establish LRFN2 as an integral protein that conforms to the dogma of SNX27-mediated membrane trafficking in that it requires SNX27 for its retrieval from lysosomal degradation, a pre-requisite for recycling back to the cell surface.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: Research on LRFN2 has principally focused on its ability to cluster NMDA receptors.
claims.source: For LRFN2, research has principally focused on its ability to cluster NMDA receptors (Wang et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2006.

claims.claim: Points of overlap exist between the distribution of cell surface LRFN2 and endogenous GluA1 and GluA2 in dendrites.
claims.source: This revealed points of overlap between the distribution of cell surface LRFN2 and endogenous GluA1 and GluA2 in dendrites (Figure 4A and B and C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A, B, and C.

claims.claim: LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 were all able to associate with GluA1 and GluA2.
claims.source: Twenty-four hr later GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation (targeting the SEP tag) and western analysis revealed that LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 were all able to associate with GluA1 and GluA2 (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Deletion of the LRR and Ig domains of LRFN2 led to a reduction in binding to GluA1 (an approximate 56% reduction) and GluA2 (an approximate 67% reduction).
claims.source: While full-length LRFN2 associated with GluA1 and GluA2, deletion of the LRR and Ig domains led to a reduction in binding (an approximate 56% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.3, p = 0.0173; and an approximate 67% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 10.6, p = <0.0001) that was further reduced upon removal of the juxtamembrane fibronectin type III domain (an approximate 79% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 12.8, p = <0.0001; and an approximate 94% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 40.5, p = <0.0001) (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Removal of the juxtamembrane fibronectin type III domain further reduced binding to GluA1 (an approximate 79% reduction) and GluA2 (an approximate 94% reduction).
claims.source: While full-length LRFN2 associated with GluA1 and GluA2, deletion of the LRR and Ig domains led to a reduction in binding (an approximate 56% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.3, p = 0.0173; and an approximate 67% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 10.6, p = <0.0001) that was further reduced upon removal of the juxtamembrane fibronectin type III domain (an approximate 79% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 12.8, p = <0.0001; and an approximate 94% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 40.5, p = <0.0001) (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: LRFN2 and AMPA receptors show overlapping distributions on the cell surface of dendrites.
claims.source: Taken together, this data demonstrates that LRFN2 and AMPA receptors show overlapping distributions on the cell surface of dendrites, and that LRFN2 associates with the GluA1 and GluA2 subunits of AMPA receptors through an interaction principally mediated by its extracellular LRR and Ig domains.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: LRFN2 associates with the GluA1 and GluA2 subunits of AMPA receptors through an interaction principally mediated by its extracellular LRR and Ig domains.
claims.source: Taken together, this data demonstrates that LRFN2 and AMPA receptors show overlapping distributions on the cell surface of dendrites, and that LRFN2 associates with the GluA1 and GluA2 subunits of AMPA receptors through an interaction principally mediated by its extracellular LRR and Ig domains.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: SNX27 suppression caused a significant reduction in cell surface GluA1 staining (an approximate 16% reduction).
claims.source: Consistent with the aforementioned biochemical analysis this revealed a significant reduction in cell surface GluA1 and GluA2 staining upon SNX27 suppression (GluA1: an approximate 16% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (730), p = 0.0003; GluA2: an approximate 34% reduction n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (632), p < 0.0001) (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: SNX27 suppression caused a significant reduction in cell surface GluA2 staining (an approximate 34% reduction).
claims.source: Consistent with the aforementioned biochemical analysis this revealed a significant reduction in cell surface GluA1 and GluA2 staining upon SNX27 suppression (GluA1: an approximate 16% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (730), p = 0.0003; GluA2: an approximate 34% reduction n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (632), p < 0.0001) (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: The suppression of LRFN2 expression caused a significant reduction in GluA2 surface expression (an approximate 40% reduction).
claims.source: In a parallel analysis, the suppression of LRFN2 expression (Figure 5B) also caused a significant reduction in GluA2 surface expression (an approximate 40% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (556), p < 0.0001) but, interestingly, had no significant effect on the cell surface expression of GluA1 (n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (1228), p = 0.8813) (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The suppression of LRFN2 expression had no significant effect on the cell surface expression of GluA1.
claims.source: In a parallel analysis, the suppression of LRFN2 expression (Figure 5B) also caused a significant reduction in GluA2 surface expression (an approximate 40% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (556), p < 0.0001) but, interestingly, had no significant effect on the cell surface expression of GluA1 (n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (1228), p = 0.8813) (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was significantly increased after suppression of SNX27 (an approximate 43% increase).
claims.source: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was quantified in the cell body and proximal dendrites and found to be significantly increased after suppression of both SNX27 (an approximate 43% increase, n = 58, Mann Whitney test, U (827), p < 0.0001) and LRFN2 (an approximate 14% increase, n = 58, Mann Whitney test, U (1198), p = 0.0073) with the GluA2 overlapping with both VPS35 and LAMP1 (Figure 6A, B, C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A, B, C.

claims.claim: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was significantly increased after suppression of LRFN2 (an approximate 14% increase).
claims.source: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was quantified in the cell body and proximal dendrites and found to be significantly increased after suppression of both SNX27 (an approximate 43% increase, n = 58, Mann Whitney test, U (827), p < 0.0001) and LRFN2 (an approximate 14% increase, n = 58, Mann Whitney test, U (1198), p = 0.0073) with the GluA2 overlapping with both VPS35 and LAMP1 (Figure 6A, B, C).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A, B, C.

claims.claim: Suppression of SNX27 or LRFN2 perturbs the recycling of GluA2, increasing its retention time in the endo-lysosomal system.
claims.source: This suggests that suppression of SNX27 or LRFN2 perturbs the recycling of GluA2, increasing its retention time in the endo-lysosomal system.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: SNX27 shRNA treatment profoundly decreased excitatory synaptic transmission compared to the non-targeting control shRNA.

results.result: Proteomic analysis of SNX27 in rat cortical neurons identified 212 high-confidence interacting proteins, including established interactors (retromer, WASH complex) and novel cargoes with neuronal functions. Sixteen proteins contained optimal Type I PDZ binding motifs, with seven being integral membrane proteins including SLC1A3, SLC4A7, SLC6A11, KCNT2, KIDINS220, ADAM22, and LRFN2.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C33 describe a systematic proteomic screen with appropriate controls (GFP-SNX27 localization to endosomes, C27), stringent filtering criteria (log-fold change >2, p<0.05, C28-C29), validation through known interactors (C30), and gene ontology analysis (C31). The identification of PDZ-binding motif-containing proteins (C32-C33) is well-supported by the methodology and includes appropriate citations for motif requirements.

results.result: AMPA receptor subunits were not detected as high-confidence SNX27 interactors in the proteomic screen, and multiple independent co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293T cells and primary neurons failed to detect direct binding between SNX27 and AMPA receptor subunits (GluA1-4), suggesting SNX27-dependent AMPA receptor recycling is principally controlled by indirect binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C40 present converging negative evidence from multiple experimental approaches: proteomics (C34-C35), co-IP in HEK293T cells with human SNX27 (C36-C37), co-IP with rat SNX27 (C38), and co-IP in primary neurons (C39). Positive controls (SLC1A3, SLC4A7) validate the experimental approach (C36). The conclusion of indirect binding (C40) is appropriately cautious and supported by citation to prior ITC data.

results.result: LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 directly associate with SNX27 through their C-terminal PDZ binding motifs. The SNX27 PDZ domain binds the LRFN2 PDZ binding motif with Kd=1.6 µM, enhanced to Kd<1.0 µM by VPS26. This interaction was confirmed with endogenous LRFN2 in primary neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 provide multiple lines of evidence: co-IP experiments showing PDZ-motif dependence (C45-C47), direct binding measurements by ITC with quantitative affinity values (C48-C49), and validation with endogenous proteins in neurons (C50). The mutagenesis experiments (C47) and VPS26 enhancement (C49) are consistent with established SNX27 binding mechanisms and include appropriate citations.

results.result: SNX27 suppression leads to reduced total and surface levels of LRFN2 (~50% total, ~52% surface) and increased LRFN2 colocalization with lysosomes (~27% increase), consistent with LRFN2 requiring SNX27 for retrieval from lysosomal degradation. SNX27 suppression also reduced surface GluA1 (~37%) and GluA2 (~64%) without affecting transferrin receptor.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C59 present a coherent trafficking story with appropriate controls (transferrin receptor, C56), statistical analysis (unpaired t-tests with reported n, t, and p values), and consistency with established SNX27 cargo behavior (C53 cites Steinberg et al., 2013). The colocalization data (C52, C58) and surface biotinylation experiments (C54-C57) use complementary approaches. The conclusion (C59) appropriately synthesizes the data.

results.result: LRFN2 shows overlapping surface distribution with AMPA receptors in dendrites and associates with GluA1 and GluA2 subunits. This association is principally mediated by the extracellular LRR and Ig domains of LRFN2, with deletion of these domains reducing binding by ~56-67%, and further deletion of the fibronectin III domain reducing binding by ~79-94%.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C66 combine imaging data showing spatial overlap (C61) with biochemical co-IP experiments (C62) and systematic domain deletion analysis (C63-C64) with appropriate statistical testing (unpaired t-tests, n=4, with reported statistics). The progressive reduction in binding with sequential deletions provides strong evidence for the domain requirements. The conclusions (C65-C66) are appropriately supported by the data.

results.result: SNX27 suppression reduced surface expression of both GluA1 (~16%) and GluA2 (~34%), while LRFN2 suppression specifically reduced GluA2 surface expression (~40%) without affecting GluA1, suggesting differential regulation of AMPA receptor subunits.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C70 use immunofluorescence with appropriate non-parametric statistics (Mann-Whitney U test, n=50) and include proper controls. The differential effect of LRFN2 on GluA2 vs GluA1 (C69-C70) is particularly interesting and well-supported by the statistical analysis (p<0.0001 for GluA2, p=0.8813 for GluA1). This is consistent with the biochemical data and suggests subunit-specific mechanisms.

results.result: Suppression of SNX27 or LRFN2 increased internalized GluA2 intensity in the cell body and proximal dendrites (~43% and ~14% increases respectively), with GluA2 colocalizing with both endosomal (VPS35) and lysosomal (LAMP1) markers, suggesting perturbed recycling and increased retention in the endo-lysosomal system.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C73 use appropriate trafficking assays with pulse-chase labeling and colocalization with organelle markers. The statistical analysis is appropriate (Mann-Whitney test, n=58) and the interpretation (C73) is cautious and consistent with the data. The differential magnitude of effects (SNX27 > LRFN2) is consistent with SNX27 having additional cargoes beyond LRFN2.

results.result: In vivo suppression of SNX27 or LRFN2 in rat hippocampus reduced excitatory synaptic transmission (measured by fEPSPs), with SNX27 producing a larger effect than LRFN2. LRFN2 suppression also attenuated hippocampal LTP induction, indicating LRFN2 plays an important role in functional AMPA receptor expression and synaptic activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C81 present ex vivo electrophysiology data with appropriate experimental design (lentiviral injection, 6-8 week expression, contralateral controls) and statistical analysis (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA for input-output curves, paired t-tests for LTP). The LTP data (C78-C80) shows robust potentiation in controls (p=0.011) but not in LRFN2 knockdown (p=0.15), supporting the conclusion. The comparison between SNX27 and LRFN2 effects (C76) is appropriately cautious.

results.result: The SNX27 neuronal interactome includes proteins linked to various neurological conditions: SLC1A3 and SLC4A7 (glutamate neurotoxicity), SLC6A11 (GABAergic tone), KCNT2 (epileptic encephalopathies), KIDINS220 (spastic paraplegia and intellectual disability), and ADAM22 (epilepsy with auditory features).
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C33, C83-C88 appropriately cite published literature linking each identified protein to specific neurological functions and diseases. These claims provide important context for understanding SNX27-associated pathologies and are well-supported by the citations. However, the functional significance of these interactions for SNX27-mediated pathology would require additional experimental validation.

results.result: SNX27 is an endosomal sorting protein containing a PDZ domain that binds both retromer and PDZ-binding motifs on cargo proteins, regulating their recycling to the plasma membrane. SNX27 dysfunction is linked to Down's syndrome and various neuropathologies, with established roles in trafficking AMPA, NMDA, serotonin receptors, and GIRK channels.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C9-C23 provide essential background information that is well-supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These claims establish the known functions of SNX27 and the rationale for the current study. All statements are appropriately referenced and represent established knowledge in the field.

results.result: Prior work by Clairfeuille and colleagues using isothermal titration calorimetry failed to detect quantifiable binding between SNX27 and AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2, even with GluA1 phosphorylation or VPS26 association, which normally enhances SNX27 binding to other cargoes.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C26 accurately cite prior published work (Clairfeuille et al., 2016) that provides important context for the current study's findings. The citation is appropriate and the description of the prior negative results is accurate. This establishes the rationale for investigating indirect mechanisms of SNX27-AMPA receptor interaction.

results.result: LRFN2 belongs to a family of five synaptic adhesion-like molecules (LRFN1-5), with LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 containing Type I PDZ binding motifs. LRFN1 and LRFN4 were detected in the raw proteomic data but filtered out because they were not quantified across all three biological replicates.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C44 provide appropriate background on the LRFN family (C41-C43, with citations to Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008) and transparently report the proteomic filtering decisions (C44). The explanation for why LRFN1 and LRFN4 were excluded from the final interactome is methodologically sound and appropriately documented.

results.result: LRFN2 and AMPA receptors are linked to various neurological and psychiatric disorders. LRFN2 is associated with antisocial personality disorder, autism, schizophrenia, working memory deficits, and learning disabilities, and shows the highest reduction among synaptic proteins in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease with dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies, correlating with cognitive decline.
results.evaluation: Claims C60, C82, C89-C95 provide important clinical and pathological context, all appropriately supported by citations to published literature. The claims about LRFN2's association with various conditions (C93-C95) and AMPA receptors' role in neurological disorders (C89-C92) establish the translational relevance of the findings. All statements are properly referenced.

results.result: SNX27 controls AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and plasticity indirectly through sorting of LRFN2. Suppression of SNX27 reduces LRFN2 expression, leading to loss of surface GluA2 expression and reduced synaptic activity, providing a new mechanism for AMPA receptor regulation and insight into SNX27- and LRFN2-associated neurological conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C8, C96-C97 represent the main conclusions of the study, synthesizing the experimental findings into a coherent model. These conclusions are well-supported by the collective evidence from proteomics, biochemistry, cell biology, and electrophysiology experiments. The claims appropriately acknowledge this as an 'additional mechanism' (C8, C97) rather than the sole mechanism, recognizing the complexity of AMPA receptor regulation.
